cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: test coverage sits at 31%, there is no coverage gate in continuous integration, and production systems of comparable complexity typically run 40-60% coverage.
cases.output: Test coverage sits at 31%, with no coverage gate in continuous integration. That is below the 40 to 60% typically observed in production systems of comparable complexity, and it means a regression can reach production unchallenged.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: deployments are performed manually by one engineer via SSH, there is no rollback procedure, and the last rollback attempt (8 months ago) took over 3 hours to complete.
cases.output: The most recent rollback attempt, 8 months ago, took over 3 hours to complete, and deployments are performed manually by a single engineer via SSH with no documented rollback procedure. This creates a single point of failure with no mitigation underway. A regression reaching production would depend entirely on one person's availability and manual recovery steps that have never been validated since the last attempt. We recommend establishing an automated deployment and rollback process, with at least one other engineer trained and able to execute it.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: one engineer holds sole access to the production database credentials, there is no documented access-handover process, and that engineer is on a rolling month-to-month contract.
cases.output: The production database credentials are held by a single engineer with no documented access-handover process, and that engineer works on a rolling month-to-month contract. If the engineer departs unexpectedly, the company loses immediate access to production data and cannot restore service without delay. There is no compensating control. This configuration creates a critical single point of failure in the availability and recoverability of the platform.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no deletion policy, and there is no documented process for handling a data-subject deletion request.
cases.output: Customer personal data is retained indefinitely, with no documented deletion policy or process for handling data-subject deletion requests. This absence of a retention schedule means records persist beyond any legitimate business need, and a subject access request for deletion cannot be fulfilled through defined steps. The company has no compensating control. Regulatory frameworks including GDPR and CCPA impose obligations to delete personal data on request, and noncompliance exposes the company to enforcement action and statutory damages.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) covering ALL of these facts: test coverage is 31%, there is no CI coverage gate, the last three production incidents were caused by untested edge cases, deployments are manual, and there is no rollback procedure. Do not omit any fact.
cases.output: Test coverage sits at 31%, with no coverage gate in continuous integration. The 3 production incidents in the past year were each caused by untested edge cases that passed through to customers. Deployments are performed manually without a documented rollback procedure. This combination leaves the platform exposed to regressions that reach production undetected and cannot be quickly reversed.

cases.input: Write three separate due-diligence findings, one paragraph each, clearly separated by a blank line. Finding 1 facts: passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table. Finding 2 facts: deployments are manual with no rollback procedure. Finding 3 facts: code comment style is inconsistent across the codebase, with no linting rule enforcing a convention.
cases.output:
Passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table, with no encryption in transit or at rest. This exposes customer credentials to anyone with database access and violates standard authentication practice. We recommend immediate migration to salted hashes with a strong algorithm such as bcrypt, and implementation of a secrets-management system for any stored credentials.

Deployments are performed manually with no documented or tested rollback procedure. The absence of rollback capability means a problematic release cannot be recovered without manual intervention and extended downtime. We recommend establishing an automated deployment pipeline with a rollback routine that is exercised in each pre-production cycle.

Code comment style is inconsistent across the codebase, with no linting rule enforcing a convention. Inconsistency increases the effort required to review and maintain unfamiliar code, and it masks whether inline documentation is present or absent. We recommend adopting a comment convention, encoding it in the linter configuration, and running the check in continuous integration.
